5-methylTHF, the essential folate

co-factor that provides methyl groups for S-adenosylmethionine-mediated methylation reactions (Bailey et al., 2015). The common
677C/T variant in the MTHFR gene is associated with reduced MTHFR enzyme function, resulting in lower blood folate and higher
homocysteine concentrations, and an increased nutritional requirement for folate. In addition, in individuals with the variant
MTHFR 677TT genotype, poor folate status causes an altered distribution of intracellular folate cofactors and reduced global meth-
ylation of DNA. Riboﬂavin also plays an important role in affected individuals because the variant enzyme binds its cofactor FAD
with lower afﬁnity, however in vivo studies show that this can be stabilized by intervention with supplemental riboﬂavin (McNulty
et al., 2002, 2006).
Several studies showed that the MTHFR 677C/T polymorphism is strongly associated with an increased of NTDs. One meta-
analysis concluded that the variant MTHFR 677TT genotype in the child or mother is associated with a doubling in the risk of NTD
(Yang et al., 2015). The frequency of the variant TT genotype is 10% worldwide, however, the distribution varies considerably
according to geographical area, ranging 0–3% (in Africa), 8–11% (in Australia), 3–18% (in United States), 8–20% (in China)
and 4–26% (in Europe). The highest reported frequencies of the TT genotype worldwide is in Mexico (32%) and speciﬁcally
